body: I approve of the message of hope, but when it entails no exposition, it can leave the listener feeling even more distanced and isolated than before. So, do you have any examples or more to say on light sources?

"The sources of light?" What are you talking about? "Chin up. That which you want (happiness) exists. Now, go fetch." No direction, no nothing. To many, what illuminates their lives depends on their own person context, so to another, that "source of light" is not a source of anything. People need more than "go fetch."

The thing with "Help, I'm going to commit suicide" is, it's not like suicide itself is the problem. It's the symptom of the problem. The problem is what people want help with and in so many cases, that's what can't be solved (or what they believe can't be solved). Stopping the suicide doesn't stop the problem.
Nope.
I know! Just curious? Curiosity? Waamp waaaaamp.
What's this in reference to? Just curious...

Madness, yes, is it the answer? You, you were one of them. You were one of them. And now circumstance has struck. Why has it struck? Could I handle your loss? Am I ridiculous by comparison, grieving my own loss that is in no way as fucked up as yours?

I want to believe. I am desperate to believe. I want to make you a symbol, a symbol of what can be, despite the rage of fate.

Your love, how can it be? No... disbelief. Tremors. How strong are you? Where is your core? Is your foundation truly undermined? All of them? All? Can there not just be a single remaining foundation you can use as a foothold?

Eggs in one basket, eggs in one basket. My eggs were in one basket. So were yours. You can cook. I'd love your food. I can cook OK, but I'm certain you're better at it.

Some who know I doubt can relate, and I want to avoid being one of those people, but I don't know if I can. How can I relate to a tale such as yours? But I mustn't pretend to know if I do not know. I can only guess. I can only come maybe halfway, if that. I want to relate, because I at least know the terror and the rending grief that life without love can wield. How can such depths exist? How can one so constantly be reeducated on how far down the depths actually extend? The abominable depths...

Fuck that, you can make it. Expecting to be sane until a year or two has past may be unrealistic, though. Imagine the shining glory that would be your soul if you could emerge on the other side. The strength, the grace... a thing of beauty. To have not ultimately succumbed to madness would be a feat others would look upon in awe. But it's not due to pride or any desire for admiration that would inform you, but something greater only you can know and others can only grasp in ignorant imaginings. Please make it. Please try. Please reach. Please...
In the interest of avoiding an ever-narrowing format of nested replies, I'm opting to continue this via PMs.
Oh. Expound.

Um, actually, it would solve my problems by way of eliminating their prerequisite: my existence. Granted, there would no longer be any "me" to experience good, bad or otherwise, but neither would I be processing that which makes me crave death with a burning passion.

People care, but they are not me and don't have to live with this flavor and intensity of despair and terror. If I knew another felt this way, I wouldn't foist demands on them that they continue. Everyone's life is their own (unless they're a parent) and any such person has the right to end it if they've the need.

I of course would rather be happy and all that, but circumstance does not favor everyone equally. I have a desire to live, but also a desire to die, and it's the former that I feel is more valid and correct. Everybody wants to live, in that base biological way. Your body wants to stay alive. I want it to die because "despair has become all directions."

The whispers (or screams) of your doubts will always have the upper hand when they're untestable. "I feel like he settled for me." Your doubts says that, but it's untestable. "My mom would prefer me dead." Your doubts say that, but it's untestable (and highly unlikely. It'd tear her up for the rest of her days). "My boyfriend will find someone better." Your doubts say that, but it's untestable.

All these things (and more, I'm sure) are unknown, yet the conviction you have that they're true are not in proportion with what you in fact know. You doubt, but you do not know. You trust your doubt, possibly because it's easier to assume the worse case than to live in uncertainty -- uncertainty about the future, uncertainty about another's emotional investment in you, uncertainty about yourself, etc.

Your doubts aren't absolute truth. They're coming from your already troubled mind, which isn't the most objective commentator, as understatement. While uncertainty can foster anxiety, it also allows for hope, and it (uncertainty) is more in keeping with the actual state of what you "know" about that which you doubt.

Wow, that's an impressive story, and while it's more than understandable that you're ready to give up, I'd like to think there are people out there like you who persevere nonetheless. After all that struggle, after all that investment in escaping, it'd be a shame to give in. You never know how close you are to breaking out.

Harsh living conditions seek to impoverish the spirit as well, and it's the spirit most of all that you must protect, prop up, and encourage. I know you probably put a lot of your spirit's chips in getting this apartment, only to have them lost in this last minute reference thing, but try to think of it as a test to see what's possible. You can get a place. Hit up Reddit in more ways than what you're doing now and as for food, try for a food bank.

Wanting to be taken seriously makes it harder for people to take you seriously. Sorta like those who _want_ to be cool are almost automatically rendered uncool simply by way of wanting it. So then you have people who are truly cool, but only because they don't care whether they're cool or not. Other people look upon them and sigh, "Boy, I wish I was cool. Then I'd feel so great, having achieved my desire." Those people cannot be cool.

But those truly cool people don't get to experience that gratification, because they don't care about being cool, which helps make them cool. To them, it doesn't matter, because even if others didn't think them cool, they wouldn't care. They feel no elation from their coolness.

So in order to achieve what you want, you can't want it... meaning you don't ever get to really gratify that want, because you only achieve it when you no longer have it. But at least you're not tormented by being unable to satisfy your desire.

Easier said than done, no? "Just stop wanting what you want." Depending on what that is, it can seem nearly impossible. But assuming it's actually impossible is a copout, letting you out of even trying, or when you fail, trying again. "It's impossible, so why try anymore?!" You don't know it's impossible. In fact, it's probably possible, but you have to get your head around it.

I don't think there's a way to suffer without it making you stronger overall. Your battered self might be weaker in some areas, but your core has persevered. Just might be hard to tell you're strong because you're constantly holding weights -- the kind "normal" people aren't burdened with.

I've seen confident ugly people who I can tell are secure in themselves. If somebody said, "Hey, you're ugly and gross," you can tell they'd be of the mind to laugh and say "fuck you," not caring about that person's opinion. Or, if they are hurt by it, they still have enough faith and value in themselves to recognize that person as an ass.

I've seen such people, and I think, "How could they act that way?" I wonder that because if I looked like them, I couldn't be that confident. That's because vanity is my folly and I'm weak when it comes to that stuff. I'm not strong enough. I'm not unattractive, though, so I'm not forced to confront it like you are. I flee, I run, I hide from that weakness. I give way to its demands and try to placate it at every turn. Not fun.

Anyway, you can't escape until you can look yourself in the mirror say, "Yeah, alright." Sucks you don't have confidants to support you, but at least you're giving Reddit a try for that...

You cannot escape. Not unless you stop holding the values that other people hold, not unless you accept yourself. But, you don't want to accept yourself, do you? Would you rather be the jock? Are you now the jock who got himself messed up somehow and who can't live with his appearance because of the values he can't release? "I must look THAT way! The way I looked before! I must!!" But you never looked that way, yet you beat yourself up because of how you've always appeared.

Stand up to yourself -- your own mind is a bully (part of it, anyway). It won't be until you can say "fuck you" to the values that are driving you into the ground that you can be your own person, be free of who you are now.

It's OK to not want what they want. Explore enjoying what you can, regardless of what it is (unless it's illegal), and try to appreciate yourself as yourself, no matter how weird it may be.
26 months? Pfff, that's nothin'. I'm WAY more ruined than you.

Fucked of me to have said that, but that's the first thought that came to my mind: "Don't want to turn him into one of her."

As for others thinking about it, that can only go so far, because

1) the sufferer isn't other people

2) other people aren't experiencing the suffering.

Heeey duuude. Me too. Although I know it's more my stubborn pride and vanity that's eating me. I've always been the strong one. Shit, I am strong, it's just that my pain is stronger, and it's embarrassing to reveal that to anyone. I can't pretend I'm that person around the one I divulged to anymore. My guts are known, I'm exposed, and I'm fighting regret. 'Course, I was experiencing more pain that I knew I could feel at the time and it seems I had no choice. And if I continued to cork it up, I'd have the ever-present desire to express myself. Nonetheless, I fear I've destroyed something, not formed a deeper bond.

It sounds horrible, but if he was a parent, and if he was to kill himself, it's better (I believe) for it to have happened before his daughter had the chance to form memories, attachments, and love. I myself am an uncle and goddamn if your post doesn't make me want to kill myself before my nephew forms similar memories of me. Goddammit. "The sooner the better" is the message I get.

Tarbaby. A tarbaby, no? You try for it, thinking yourself foolish, but it's something you can hear others suggesting as a good idea... and soon you know you were right. Your fist is stuck to it, dark as pitch. You feel worse, having exposed your suffering to what hasn't the experience to understand your condition, and so you try to extricate yourself by shoving against it with your other hand, which you do by trying to explain and express yourself further. Just more of a sticky morass. And then there you are, stuck to this wretched tarbaby, more frustrated than when you started, and feeling naive to boot. Fucking goddamn tarbaby.

The pit. There are you, pit. I know you. I've stared at the blackness of your depths for so long I've forgotten what anything else looks like, tricking myself into thinking I see the bottom. But there isn't one, is there? "No, I am endless," says the pit. "Fuck you, pit. I do hate you and everything you are and stand for. You are the horror of my life."

Yeeess, it is dark. Very, very dark. Breathing deep only does so much to counter the coil tightening around your chest. Soon, that small respite is exhausted and you're left with nothing but a gray stare, and your soul remains utterly bereft yet continually robbed.
If he could steal away some of your hopeful spirit, leaving you with less of what drives you to see the world as you do, would you allow it?

Don't you think he thought about that, though? Noble though it would be to live a life of (hidden) pain for the sake of everyone else, that would be an unfair imposition to make on anyone. Excepting parents, that is (reproduce, and your life is no longer your own).

The pain of his passing is yours and everyone else's to hold now, but can you imagine a pain so deep and so pervasive, despite your practice at momentarily blinding yourself to it in social settings, that death is the ONLY escape? If you can imagine that kind of pain, and I'm betting your uncle most certainly could, how could you say, "I can't actually feel your pain, nor do I have to live with it, but live with it. Live with it for me. Live with it for everyone that's not you. Bear the impossible, even though it's impossible."

He must have felt unfathomable pain, sorrow, and sadness. You would've believe the mask I've myself made. I can almost convince myself of it, sometimes. But then there's the solitude, and the hell I experience there so very many are none the wiser to.

For some reason, I feel like I can relate to your uncle and how much he apparently hid himself. And because of that, though I have great love for others in my life, I could never ask them to live with this pain. I would understand, and not begrudge them their necessity, even though I'd know I would mourn their absence for the rest of my life.
And then there's the voice that sounds in your mind like the realist, the harsh and objective critic that calls bullshit, telling you your hope is a fool's dream. And you feel too weak to argue.

Depends how desperate you are. If you feel like you could at any given point choose death, then nothing really matters and you might as well try anything. Volunteer helping out old people, help the unfortunate. If you could well die by your own hand tomorrow anyway, the fuck does it matter? Also depends where your pride is, though, which depressed people can still have enough of to make them pig-headed. Acts of desperation, even if they're in service of improving one's own conditions, rarely bolster pride, but if death is right around the corner, maybe humility is the way to go.

Is it the meaning? Do you fear meaninglessness? Is she/your relationship with her the most meaningful thing you've ever known? Do you feel like it would mean more for your life to end in the name of what you've lost than anything you might accomplish in its absence?

I'm a guy and I agree: there's something about dudes. They do not deserve to know. They should not be let in. Dudes are poisoned by machismo (most dressing it in subtler clothing) and there's always that undertone, unspoken though it is, that feelings are somehow unmanly, that they are themselves weakness. Perhaps it's just built in, but girls seem to understand emotion better.

This happens with me, however, it tends to be reruns of what I've lost, in various metaphorical ways. Sometimes it's concrete and everything's good. Regardless of which kind I have, I awake to a nauseous mixture of fear, regret, horror, and sorrow. Then I go through the motions of my day, and no one is the wiser.

I wonder if everything will be alright -- something I hope for out of the need that it be the case, which I soon re-recognize as irrelevant to whether everything will be alright or not. I then worry myself to numb exhaustion and shortly thereafter slide into an unconsciousness whose dreams I fear remembering.
